@RepFeenstra Thank you, Rep. Feenstra, for supporting the continuation of audio-only telehealth! Access to healthcare is essential, and this legislation will make a real difference for families, farmers, and seniors. Let's ensure everyone has the care they need when they need it!

Rep. Randy Feenstra's push to extend Medicare coverage for audio-only telehealth is a smart move to protect seniors and rural residents who rely on phone-based care. During the COVID-19 pandemic, nearly half of Medicare beneficiaries used virtual visits, proving its necessity. 

The American Relief Act (2025) temporarily extended these services, but without permanent legislation, Medicare will revert to outdated restrictions. Feenstra’s bill, unlike the weak bipartisan efforts, directly addresses the looming "telehealth cliff" and ensures continued access to essential care, especially for behavioral health and chronic disease management. 

Congress must act decisively to prevent disruption.

Rural healthcare is essential, but let’s not pretend throwing more taxpayer $$$ at bloated programs fixes systemic waste. The GAO’s latest report flags healthcare programs as high-risk for mismanagement, with $233B-$521B lost annually to fraud. 

Jackson’s bill removes mileage limits for critical access hospitals—good for rural coverage, but without strict audits, it’s a blank check for bureaucrats. The previous administration burned $881M on useless education contracts; this bill needs airtight safeguards to prevent similar waste. 

Prioritize care, not bureaucracy.

Rural hospital closures hit hardest where government bloat hits hardest. Since 2010, 136 rural hospitals shuttered while HHS spending ballooned from $1.2T to $1.7T annually. The problem isn’t funding shortages—it’s bureaucratic mismanagement.

Redirecting just 1% of HHS’s budget could save every at-risk facility. Real solutions require slashing administrative fat, not just writing bigger checks to a broken system.
